# Eliza Pullen

## Overview

- **Age:** 57 years old  <sub>[v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P29](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0029)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P26](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0026)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_

## Appearance

Eliza Pullen maintains a severe appearance. By Volume 2, her overall look has become even more austere than normal.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014)_

## Personality

Eliza Pullen is characterized by a deeply ingrained pessimistic outlook. Her pervasive negativity causes others to view her as notably defeatist.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P60](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0060), [v2 XVII A Chapter of Accidents P64](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0064)_

## Traits

- defeatist  <sub>[v2 XVII A Chapter of Accidents P64](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0064)</sub>

## History

Eliza Pullen lived with her sister Catherine in a small brown dwelling located in a sunlit spot within Mark Andrew's beech forest, where they had been known as the Andrew sisters for over fifty years. When [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Isolde visited their home to canvas for the [Brierley](../codex/places.md#brierley) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers), Eliza bitterly refused to make a donation.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P12](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0012), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P16](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0016), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P30](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0030), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P31](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0031)_

## Quotes

> "The need for it escapes me. When we were young, Catherine Pullen, we did not go gallivanting to halls and such locations. With each passing day, this world deteriorates."
>
> — Eliza Pullen — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P18](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0018)

> "Medical men perpetually speak in that manner merely to maintain folks' spirits. Were I in her place, I would not possess great expectations. One ought to be ready for the most dreadful outcome."
>
> — Eliza Pullen — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P27](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0027)

> "Are you leaving? Well, it is my hope that your new society can prevent Brierley from slipping any lower, though my expectations are small."
>
> — Eliza Pullen — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P29](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0029)

> "You won’t hold it in such high regard once you’ve spent as much time in it as I have,"
>
> — Eliza Pullen — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P24](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0024)

> "I have not found that to be true, and my fifty-seven years outweigh your sixteen,"
>
> — Eliza Pullen — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P29](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0029)
